stem: A 7-year-old boy has brief, repeated shoulder jerks and throat-clearing noises during class, and he says he feels an uncomfortable sensation just before they happen; which feature most strongly supports a tic rather than an epileptic seizure?

options.text: An associated premonitory urge before the event
They involve more than one body part
They occur repeatedly through the day

explanation: An associated premonitory urge before the event is the feature that most strongly supports a tic. This uncomfortable urge is a classic clue for tics and helps distinguish them from epileptic seizures.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because a premonitory urge is a classic feature of tics and strongly supports the diagnosis.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because non-rhythmic movements can occur in tics, but this is less specific than a premonitory urge.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because tics may be simple or complex, so involving more than one body part does not best distinguish them.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because repeated episodes through the day can occur in several paroxysmal conditions and are not specific.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because brief events can occur in both tics and seizures, so brevity alone is not discriminating.
